Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached are Arcadia's redlines for the MSA and the Order Form focused on SLA and support language. High-level items we want to resolve before legal can clear: 

- Uptime target: request 99.95% availability for the API endpoints used in production (your draft is 99.9%).
- Service credits: propose a 100% credit for any month where uptime falls below 99.5% and a sliding scale down to 10% for minor breaches (we included a table).

We've flagged a few sections in the attached Word redline (Arcadia-Redlines_MSA.docx) and exported a clean PDF of the Order Form changes. Folks — forwarding Arcadia's redlines (see attached). They landed firm asks on uptime, credits, response times, and maintenance notice. Quick thoughts:

- Uptime: 99.95% vs our standard 99.9% will materially shift economics for Dedicated and Hosted. We should treat embeddings/aux endpoints differently if needed.
- Credits: their 100% cap for <99.5% is a non-starter as written; we can consider a graded credit schedule but need a hard cap (recommend max one month invoice as cap).
- Response times: 1h initial for Sev1 is okay for enterprise if paired with higher-priority routed support (Dedicated customers); need to define what qualifies as Sev1.
- Maintenance: 72h notice is longer than our current 48h; we can agree to 72h for changes that impact production SLAs but need flexibility for urgent security patches.

Asks: Dev — can you propose redline language for credits cap, notification exceptions (security hotfix), and a clear Sev1 definition? Marissa — can you prepare a commercial counter that shows impact to unit economics if we move to 99.95 for their primary endpoints and propose a mixed SLA: 99.95 for inference API, 99.9 for embeddings? Laura — ops input on maintenance cadence and whether a 4h single-window cap is operationally feasible.

I told Jenna we'll get back with legal/commercial positions and a proposed timeslot for a call. Available windows: Mon 10/2 10–12 PT (tentative) or Tue 11/2 14–16 PT.

Thanks — Soojin

Hi team — I reviewed Arcadia's redlines and sketched out proposed language. High level: we should be flexible on targets but firm on economics and operational exceptions. Key proposed points to insert into the MSA/Order Form redline: 

1) Availability tiers: Define endpoints in the Order Form ("Core Inference API" vs "Auxiliary Services") so mutually agreed endpoints can carry different uptime targets. Default: 99.9% for all services; for named Core endpoints client may request 99.95% subject to a surcharge and capacity planning acknowledgement.

2) Service credits: Graded scale with a hard cap equal to the monthly recurring charges (one month's invoice). Example: >=99.9% — no credits; 99.0–99.9% — 10% credit; 98.0–99.0% — 30% credit; <98.0% — 50% credit. We should avoid 100% credit to limit indemnity exposure.

3) Response & Escalation: Define "Sev 1" specifically (total outage of production Core endpoints impacting >50% of requests or system-wide latency >5x baseline). Initial acknowledgement within 1 hour for Sev1 (during business hours for Hosted customers; 24/7 for Dedicated with paid support). Target remediation windows are commitments but not warranties; remedial credits tied to measured downtime only.

4) Maintenance & Exceptions: Agree to 72 hours notice for planned maintenance that impacts Core endpoints; allow emergency maintenance with best-effort notice for security patches. Scheduled monthly maintenance cumulative cap of 6 hours (rather than 8) is reasonable. Also add a clause that scheduled windows are excluded from uptime calculations for the affected endpoints.

I'll draft specific redline language and attach an SLA comparison table. Marissa — commercial impact numbers attached so you can propose surcharge bands for 99.95.

—Dev
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Jenna — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. We reviewed internally and can propose the following compromise to keep momentum: 

- Availability: For the Core Inference API endpoints we will offer 99.95% availability (on a 30d rolling basis) as an opt-in Order Form item. Embeddings and auxiliary endpoints will remain at 99.9% by default. Opt-in to 99.95% will require an agreed-upon monthly surcharge (details below) and a capacity planning kickoff.
- Service credits: We can accept a graded credit schedule but must cap total credits at one month's recurring charges. Proposed scale: >=99.95% — no credit; 99.90–99.95% — 10% credit; 99.50–99.90% — 30% credit; <99.50% — 50% credit.
- Response times: Sev1 initial acknowledgement within 1 hour (24/7 for Dedicated customers enrolled in Premium Support; business hours for standard Hosted). Sev2 initial response within 4 hours. We'll include definitions of Sev levels in the SLA exhibit.
- Maintenance: Limit scheduled maintenance to no more than 2 windows/month and no single window > 6 hours; scheduled windows will be excluded from availability calculations. We will provide 72 hours' notice for planned work that impacts Core endpoints; for security hotfixes we will provide notice as early as possible and exclude emergency maintenance from credit calculations.

Next steps: 
1) Dev — please add the redline for the credit cap and the emergency maintenance carve-out.
2) Laura — confirm 2 windows/month + 6h max single window works for ops.
3) Jenna — if this looks reasonable, can we book a 30m call Tues Nov 3 10:00 PT? I can bring the pricing tables (surcharge bands for 99.95). We'll share a clean Order Form showing the opt-in line items and a DocuSign link after the call.

Thanks,
